summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, John S. Strong earned degrees from Oberlin College, Hartford International University, and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. He spent his primary academic career at Bates College (~1978-2017).

Working in linguistics and Indology, John Shakespear studied under John Richardson. He held professorships in oriental languages at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805-1809) and the Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809-1829).
Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, John Shore succeeded William Jones and served as President of The Asiatic Society.

An Indologist and scholar of religion, John Stratton Hawley studied at Amherst College and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served on the faculty at Bowdoin College (~1974-1978) before becoming a professor at Columbia University (~1986).
A philosopher who studied at University College London, John Stuart Mill worked at the East India Company from approximately 1823 to 1858.

A historian who studied at the University of Cambridge and Leiden University, John Sydenham Furnivall founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1936-1941).

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, John Taber earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He taught at Case Western Reserve University (~1984-1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).

A linguist and Indologist, John Thompson Platts studied at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford. He taught at Saugor High School, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and served as Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford (1880).

Specializing in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, John Vincent Bellezza studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel. He held an affiliation with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, John W. Pettit studied at Haverford College, under Dilgo Khyentse, and under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman.

A scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, John W. Schroeder completed his degrees at the University of Oregon under Don S. Levi. He taught at the College of Wooster and St. Mary's College of Maryland (1996).
Working in Indology and history, John W. Spellman held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1964-1967) and the University of Windsor (~1967-1999).

An Indologist and linguist educated at the University of Edinburgh, John Wilson founded Wilson College, Mumbai, served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835-1842), and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

A scholar of Indology and religious studies educated at University College, Oxford, John Woodroffe served as Tagore Law Professor at the University of Calcutta, Judge of the Calcutta High Court (~1904-1922), and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (~1923-1930).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Join Saeki studied at Sennyu-ji and under Sadatomo Chihaya. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, the Imperial Academy, Hōryūji Kangakuin, and served as head of Hōryū-ji (1903-1950).
A scholar of Japanese history and Japanology, Joji Fujii studied at Kyoto University (~1966-1974) and later held an academic post there (~1989-2011).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and history, Jokai Hiraoka studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He later held posts at Shuchiin University and as professor at Otemae University (~1966-1993).

Jon Kabat-Zinn studied at Haverford College and MIT. A scholar of religious studies and other fields, he held appointments at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and UMass Chan Medical School, where he founded the Center for Mindfulness in 1979.
A philosopher and Indologist, Jonardon Ganeri studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Sussex, Monash, NYU, and the University of Toronto (~2020).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Jonathan A. Silk studied at Oberlin and the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez. He held posts at Grinnell, Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.
